title: Node.js
summary: Find the runtime version, package scripts and module rules before changing a Node.js project. npm is one package manager option, not a requirement of Node.js.

sections.label: Where config lives
sections.text: Node.js is an asynchronous event-driven JavaScript runtime. A project declares scripts, dependencies and devDependencies in package.json. The engines field declares a supported Node.js version range, rather than proving compatibility. package-lock.json describes the exact dependency tree and is intended to be committed into source repositories. ESLint 10 flat config searches from each target file's directory upward for eslint.config.js, .mjs, .cjs or supported TypeScript variants. Earlier ESLint versions can use different discovery rules. Which of these files exist is a fact about the repository, not about Node.js.

sections.label: Conventional commands
sections.text:
# Conventions, not facts about any project. Read the scripts field first.
npm ci
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
node --test

sections.label: How CI is declared
sections.text: Node.js does not declare CI, the CI system does. On GitHub Actions the workflow file lives in the .github/workflows directory, the actions/setup-node step installs the requested Node.js version, and the documented example runs npm ci and then npm test. The same page says npm ci installs the exact lockfile versions and does not update the lockfile. Other CI systems have their own file conventions, which this topic does not record.

sections.label: Where review conventions live
sections.text: Review conventions belong to the repository host, not to Node.js. Look for pull request templates, required checks and branch rules there. This topic records no review policy.

sections.label: Gotchas
items: npm ci needs a lockfile accepted by the installed npm version. npm 11 accepts package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json. npm 12 requires package-lock.json and no longer reads shrinkwrap files. A manifest mismatch fails, existing node_modules is removed first, and package.json and the lockfile are not rewritten.

In the reviewed Node.js documentation, .mjs means ES modules and .cjs means CommonJS. An explicit package.json type controls .js files. Without a controlling type, syntax detection can treat an ambiguous .js file as an ES module. Detection is enabled by default since Node.js 22.7.0 and 20.19.0. Set type explicitly.
An exports field limits imports through package subpaths, so an unlisted subpath throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. This is not a security boundary against absolute file access.
npm treats engines as advisory when installing a dependency unless engine-strict is enabled.
By default npm test runs defined pretest, test and posttest scripts, and npm run runs a named script with its matching pre and post scripts. Check script settings before assuming hooks ran.

In the reviewed Node.js 26 documentation, node --test discovers patterns including **/*.test.js and **/test/**/*.js, and TypeScript equivalents unless --no-strip-types is given. Confirm the actual runtime version before relying on these patterns.

Node.js 26 can run erasable TypeScript by stripping types without type checking. This built-in path ignores tsconfig.json and rejects syntax that needs code generation, such as enums. Earlier releases have different support and flags.
The release page says production applications should use only Active LTS or Maintenance LTS releases.

sections.label: What Atlas provides
sections.text: Selecting Node.js adds the Node.js profile questions and checks to a project. The profile does not infer commands, versions, module system or compatibility, and Atlas runs nothing.

sections.label: Check in your environment
sections.text: Confirm the installed Node.js and npm versions, the scripts field, whether a lockfile is committed, the type and engines fields, and the test runner the project uses. Every command here is a convention to confirm against that evidence.

sections.label: Review scope
sections.text: Scoped claims checked on 2026-10-12 against Node.js 26.11.1, npm 11.21.0 and 12.2.0, ESLint 10 documentation and the linked GitHub tutorial. Runtime features and discovery can differ on earlier versions. Example commands are not executed evidence and do not apply to projects that use another package manager.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow steps: Development, Tests and review, Release and production. These links are recommendations based on the guide content, not required product or process choices.
An environment note names the actual Node.js and package manager versions, package directory, scripts and module settings.
The chosen repository commands link to discovered tests and actual outputs, including hooks and skipped work. Example commands remain illustrative until confirmed.
The release evidence records dependency tree and build results for the candidate revision. Version declarations alone do not establish runtime compatibility.
Existing source claims were not re-audited in this mapping pass. Project configuration, usefulness and actual check outcomes remain unverified.

basis: Scoped official documentation and proposed project guidance
confidence: The listed factual claims were checked against their sources on 2026-10-12 within the stated version and host scope. Recommendations and example commands do not prove suitability or execution in a particular project.

catalog.applicability: Use when a project installs, tests or builds through package.json and npm scripts on Node.js.
catalog.limits: Catalogue inclusion is not an installed runtime, a verified command set or confirmed compatibility with any project.
